author: Themanfrom1982
quote:
Waited to score on my third play through. I’ve jumped from 9 to 10 solely for the polish of the game. You literally need to perform Naruto like finger movements to find any game breaking glitches, and on this third play through I discovered that the bunny hood does not simply clip through items that Link is carrying (even a certain fishy friend.) The music is slightly better than the original, the accessibility of the combat and item collection has done well for my great nieces, the control set up is finally smooth and where it needs to be. I’ve spent too much time on fishing and harassing the Guay swarms with the slingshot (which is a very good bit of fun without Z targeting on the master display mode.)
The biggest fix of the remake over the original and 3DS remaster, is the ice arrow. It is finally useful in many situations, finally making every item in this game exciting to use! With the polish of the controls, the enemy AI (the Stalfos can almost be a challenge even after all these years) and the undeniable care put to the art direction of the game, I’m rating this a ten.

The game is concise, it’s entertaining and enchanting, and still somehow in what feels like a short game, you’ll get lost repeatedly just wandering and exploring the fairy tale world of Link and Navi.

And yes, having Navi shut up was definitely the right direction.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Themanfrom1982
quote: I need to be extra clear on this scoring. If you have never played GTA, this game might be okay for you. If you instead spent 80 to 100 dollars in anticipation of the next GTA due to how much you love the gameplay and chaos of the game, you’ll score this game lower than I have. The only way to enjoy this game is to ignore the side missions and main missions after you’ve made enough progress to actually have fun with doing things like finally being allowed to steal an automobile. This is “Grand Theft Auto” after all, it’s no great sin to expect then that one would be able to steal an automobile- as it is intrinsic to the gameplay. Rather it should be. This game has been stuffed with the weirdest side missions ever seen in GTA, and no, it isn’t fluff to talk about this, because you skip relationship missions at the cost of your endgame cutscene. You may choose not to toil over the roof, the burgers, and the flowers at your own peril. You may also choose not to play this game. What you may not choose is to open fire on special protected NPCs, or drive through a group of protestors (though plowing through a beach is fair play) you may not choose to fire a weapon inside of certain locations. You may not choose to induce the chaos for which the games have become renowned for, but the game itself may in fact choose to throw you straight through the earth’s surface, ending with a chaotic respawn and instant wasted landing. If I hadn’t spent 80 dollars on it, if the weapon wheel worked as it was supposed to, if I hadn’t faced three no clipping events in my play through after vehemently going online to defend against the “misinformation” of the haters, I would definitely have given this a five. This game has taken my time reserved for enjoyment and replaced it with full on regret. I have no interest in a second play through nor do I see myself coming back after any patches and updates. I wanted GTA, so it seems I have to return to decade old game. Stay away from this and wait for the next GTA online, the story and missions are a grind to get through, and even when Online drops, I shudder to think of what that online experience will entail for the early players.
